ARG.diversity: Argentina's uniform national self-identification law masks sharp provincial variation. Buenos Aires is the progressive, tourist-facing pole — early civil-union schemes, the country's first same-sex marriages and the main trans community infrastructure sit there — while the record notes family expulsion and hostility concentrated in more socially conservative provinces. Anti-discrimination coverage has been a patchwork: only Buenos Aires city and Rosario had explicit local rules and no national statute ever passed, so protection literally depends on which municipality a visitor stands in. Enforcement varies too: documented police mistreatment of trans women clusters in capital-city operations, and the current national rollback effort is being contested in courts, meaning the practical regime shifts by province, by city and by the stance of the officials encountered.

Custody-placement standards for trans prisoners are documented only from Queensland. A visitor's regime varies more by state than by city.
